title: CHAPTER 3: LEARNING AND THEORIES OF LEARNING
content:
👋 ሰላም፤ ጤና ይስጥልን! ዛሬ የGeneral Psychology (Psyc 1011) Chapter 3 የመጨረሻውን ክፍል (Part 3) ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። በዚህ ክፍል Albert Bandura ያቀረበውን Social Learning Theory (Observational Learning)፣ የModeling አራት ደረጃዎችን፣ Educational Implications እንዲሁም Cognitive Learning Theories (Latent Learning እና Insight Learning) በስፋትና በዝርዝር እናያለን።👇👇👇


3.3.2. Social Learning Theory (Observational Learning Theory)

According to psychologist Albert Bandura, a major part of human learning consists of observational learning, which is learning by watching the behavior of another person, or model. Because of its reliance on observation of others—a social phenomenon—the perspective taken by Bandura is often referred to as a social cognitive approach to learning (Bandura, 1999, 2004).

Three Forms of Reinforcement in Observational Learning:
1. Direct Reinforcement: The observer reproduces the behaviors of the model and receives direct reinforcement/reward.
2. Vicarious Reinforcement: The observer simply sees others (the model) being reinforced for a particular behavior and then increases his or her production of that behavior.
3. Self-Reinforcement: Controlling one's own reinforcers. This sort of reinforcement is important for both students and teachers because students value and enjoy their growing competence rather than relying solely on external rewards.

Social cognitive theorists believe that in human beings, observational learning cannot be fully understood without taking into account the thought processes of the learner. They emphasize the knowledge that results when a person sees a model behaving in certain ways and experiencing the consequences.

Four Necessary Conditions for Effective Modeling:
1. Attention: The person must first pay attention to the model.
2. Retention: The observer must be able to remember the behavior that has been observed. Rehearsal is a key technique to increase retention.
3. Motor Reproduction: The third condition is the ability to replicate/reproduce the behavior that the model has just demonstrated. (For example, little children have difficulty doing complex physical motion).
4. Motivation: The final necessary ingredient for modeling to occur is motivation; learners must want to demonstrate what they have learned. Since these four conditions vary among individuals, different people will reproduce the same behavior differently.

👉 Social Learning Theory :
• Observational Learning: ሰዎችን (Models) በመመልከትና በማስተዋል የምንማረው የመማር አይነት ነው።
• Vicarious Reinforcement: ሌላ ሰው ጥሩ ነገር ሲያደርግና ሲሸለም አይተን፣ እኛም ያንን ባህሪ ለማድረግ መነሳሳት። (ለምሳሌ፡ በክፍል ውስጥ ተሳትፎ አድርጎ መምህሩ ያመሰገነውን ተማሪ አይተን እኛም መሳተፍ)።
• Self-Reinforcement: በራሳችን ስኬትና የእውቀት እድገት ደስተኛ በመሆን ራሳችንን ማበረታታት።
• የModeling 4 ደረጃዎች (ARMM): Attention (ትኩረት መስጠት) ➔ Retention (በአእምሮ መያዝ/ማስታወስ) ➔ Motor Reproduction (ድርጊቱን በተግባር ማድረግ) ➔ Motivation (ለማድረግ ፍላጎት/ሞቲቬሽን )።

😂 የሳይኮሎጂ ቀልድ ለፈገግታ: አንድ ተማሪ የBanduraን Vicarious Reinforcement ተረድቶ፡ "ጓደኛዬ ጥናት አጥንቶ 'A' ሲያመጣ አባቱ ላፕቶፕ ሲሸልመው አየሁት፤ እኔ ደግሞ እሱን በመመልከቴ ብቻ ላፕቶፑን እኩል ልንካፈል ይገባል!" ብሎ ሲጠይቅ አባቱ "አንተስ Motivation እና Motor Reproduction ላይ የለህበትም እንዴ?" አሉት ይባላል! 😂


Educational Implications of Social Learning Theory

Social learning theory has numerous implications for classroom use:
1. Students often learn a great deal simply by observing other people.
2. Describing the consequences of behavior can effectively increase appropriate behaviors and decrease inappropriate ones (discussing rewards and consequences).
3. Modeling provides an alternative to shaping for teaching new behaviors (faster and more efficient than shaping).
4. Teachers and parents must model appropriate behaviors and take care not to model inappropriate ones.
5. Teachers should expose students to a variety of other models to break down traditional stereotypes.
6. Students must believe that they are capable of accomplishing school tasks (developing a sense of Self-Efficacy). Teachers promote this through confidence-building messages and highlighting success.
7. Teachers should help students set realistic expectations for their academic accomplishments.
8. Self-regulation techniques provide an effective method for improving student behavior.

👉 የSocial Learning Theory ትምህርታዊ ጥቅሞች:
• Modeling vs Shaping: Shaping ረጅም ጊዜ የሚወስድ ሲሆን፣ Modeling ግን ሰዎችን በማሳየት በፍጥነትና በብቃት ለማስተማር ይረዳል።
• Self-Efficacy (በራስ መተማመን): ተማሪዎች "እኔ መስራት እችላለሁ" የሚል እምነት እንዲኖራቸው መርዳት።
• Self-Regulation: ተማሪዎች የራሳቸውን ባህሪና አጠናን በራሳቸው እንዲቆጣጠሩ ማድረግ።


3.3.3. Cognitive Learning Theory

Traditional classical and operant conditionings explain learning by the principle of contiguity (the close association of events in time and space). However, cognitive learning theories focus on the internal mental processes that occur during learning.

For half a century, American learning theories focused on the behavioral "ABCs" — Antecedents (events preceding behavior), Behaviors, and Consequences. In the 1940s, social learning theory modified this, and by the 1960s/1970s, cognitive learning added the human capacity for higher levels of cognitive processing. Cognitivists argue that humans have attitudes, beliefs, and expectations that affect how they acquire information, make decisions, reason, and solve problems.

Cognitive learning takes two main forms:
1. Latent Learning
2. Insight Learning (Gestalt Learning or Perceptual Learning)

👉 Cognitive Learning Theory ብያኔ:
ኮግኒቲቭ ሌርኒንግ የሚያተኩረው ከውጫዊ ባህሪ ይልቅ በአእምሮአችን ውስጥ ባሉ የአስተሳሰብ፣ የእምነት፣ የመረጃ ማቀናበርና የውሳኔ አሰጣጥ ሂደቶች (Internal Mental Processes) ላይ ነው! Behavioral ABCs የሚባሉት Antecedents፣ Behaviors እና Consequences ናቸው።


Latent Learning

'Latent' means hidden; thus, latent learning is learning that occurs but is not evident or demonstrated in behavior until later, when conditions or incentives for its appearance are favorable. It occurs without immediate reinforcement of particular responses and involves changes in how information is cognitive processed.

Tolman and Honzik's Classic Experiment (1930):
Placed three groups of rats in mazes for more than two weeks:
• Group 1: Always found food at the end of the maze (learned quickly).
• Group 2: Never found food (did not learn to reach the end).
• Group 3: Found no food for 10 days, but received food on the 11th day.
Result: On the 11th day, Group 3 rats suddenly ran to the end of the maze just as fast as Group 1! They had developed a Cognitive Map (a mental representation of the maze) during the first 10 days without reinforcement, but only demonstrated it when reward was introduced.

👉 Latent Learning (የተሸሸገ/ስውር መማር) :
• Latent Learning: ትምህርቱ በአእምሮ ውስጥ የሚከሰት ነገር ግን ወዲያውኑ በባህሪ የማይገለፅ፣ ይልቁንም ተስማሚ ሁኔታ ወይም ማበረታቻ ሲገኝ ብቻ የሚወጣ ስውር መማር ነው።
• Cognitive Map: በአእምሮ ውስጥ የሚሰራ የአካባቢ ወይም የእውቀት ካርታ/ስዕል ነው።

💡 Exam Hint: Tolman ያደረገው የአይጦች ሙከራ የሚያስረዳው Reinforcement ለመማር (Learning) የግድ አስፈላጊ እንዳልሆነ፣ ነገር ግን የተማሩትን በባህሪ ለማሳየት (Performance) እንደሚያስፈልግ ነው! ይህ የፈተና ጥያቄ ላይ በብዛት ይመጣል።


Insight Learning

Insight Learning (also known as Gestalt learning or perceptual learning) is a cognitive process whereby we reorganize our perception of a problem. It does not depend on conditioning of particular behaviors. Wolfgang Köhler's famous experiments with chimpanzees (such as Sultan using sticks and boxes to reach bananas) demonstrated this process. Sometimes, people wake up from sleep with a solution to a problem they couldn't solve during the day.

In a typical insight situation, a problem is posed, followed by a period where no apparent progress is made, and then the solution comes suddenly. Humans (and higher animals) who solve a problem insightfully experience a sudden good feeling called the 'Aha!' experience. What is learned through insight can also be easily applied to other similar situations.

👉 Insight Learning (አእምሯዊ ግንዛቤ/ቅጽበታዊ መፍትሔ) :
• Insight Learning: ችግርን በምናስብበት ጊዜ ድንገት አእምሮአችን መረጃዎችን እንደገና በማደራጀት ቅጽበታዊ መፍትሔ (Sudden Solution) የሚያገኝበት የመማር ሂደት ነው። (Wolfgang Köhler በቺምፓንዚዎች/Sultan ላይ ያደረገውን ሙከራ ያስታውሷል)።
• 'Aha!' Experience: መፍትሔው ድንገት አእምሯችን ላይ ሲመጣ የሚሰማን የደስታና የመረዳት ስሜት ነው።


Summary of Chapter 3

• Learning: A relatively permanent change in behavior occurring as a result of experience or practice.
• Characteristics: Modification of behavior, pervasive, active process, purposeful, and multifaceted.
• Principles: Categorized into 8 valuable principles guiding learning efficiency.
• Theories: Classical Conditioning (Pavlov), Operant Conditioning (Skinner), Social Learning (Bandura), and Cognitive Learning (Tolman - Latent, Kohler - Insight).
